children: Palo Alto Networks closed fiscal Q4 2026 with total revenue of $3.41 billion and next‑generation security ARR of $9.10 billion, marking strong year‑over‑year growth. The company reported a GAAP net loss of $282 million and non‑GAAP diluted net income per share of $1.02 for the quarter. Management highlighted robust platform demand, an acquisition of Console to expand agentic AI workflows, and guidance for continued ARR and revenue growth into FY27.
Total revenue for Q4 fiscal 2026: $3.41 billion (34% year over year).
Next‑Generation Security ARR (Q4 fiscal 2026): $9.10 billion (63% year over year).
Gross profit for Q4 fiscal 2026: $2,304 million (total gross profit reported; gross margin percentage not provided explicitly).
GAAP net loss for Q4 fiscal 2026: $282 million; GAAP diluted loss per share: $(0.35).
Non‑GAAP net income for Q4 fiscal 2026: $853 million; non‑GAAP diluted net income per share: $1.02.
Added nearly $1 billion of net new Next‑Generation Security ARR in the quarter, described by management as a major contributor to platform momentum.
Reported broad strength across Network & AI Security, Cortex, and Idira platforms, driving outperformance versus guidance.
Acquisition of Console to extend the Cortex platform with an AI‑native agentic workflow capability for enterprise operations.
Remaining performance obligations grew 34% year over year to $21.2 billion, indicating multi‑period contracted demand and backlog expansion.
Company reiterated multi‑year targets and provided FY27 guidance: total revenue $14.10B–$14.20B and Next‑Generation Security ARR $11.075B–$11.175B.
